title: Comparison 4 · Shift / rotate order dependency
summary: Rotate→Shift vs Shift→Rotate produce different images (R·T ≠ T·R around the image centre). Subtract to visualise the gap.

steps.title: See how operator order matters
steps.body:
Rotation and translation generally produce **different images** if you swap their order. Rotation is around the image centre, so:

  • **Rotate → Shift**: rotate around the centre first, then translate by (dy, dx) in canvas coordinates.
  • **Shift → Rotate**: translate (dy, dx) first → content is now offset from the centre; rotating lands it at R·(dy, dx) → the shift direction appears rotated by the angle.

In this tutorial we build two pipelines A / B and visualise **A − B** as a difference image. The SPIDER / RELION convention is 'rotate first, translate second' (= pipeline A's order), and you need to agree on this when propagating alignment parameters downstream.

steps.title: Drop the data node
steps.body: From Palette (Data), drag **Test · Checkerboard** (256×256). Its crisp step-edges make position shifts obvious.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.checker` shows its image before we build the two pipelines.

steps.title: Pipeline A · drop Rotate
steps.body: Build pipeline A (Rotate → Shift) first. From Geometry, drag **Rotate** (`geom.rotate`).

steps.title: Wire Checker → Rotate (A)
steps.body: Drag Checker's `image` output to Rotate's `image` input.

steps.title: Click Rotate (A)
steps.body: Click this Rotate. We'll set `angle_deg` in the Inspector.

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 30
steps.body: Enter **30** in `angle_deg`. Off-axis angles bring out the order-dependence more clearly.

steps.title: Pipeline A · drop Shift
steps.body: From Geometry, drag **Shift** (`geom.shift`). Place it after Rotate (A).

steps.title: Wire Rotate (A) → Shift (A)
steps.body: Drag Rotate's `image` output to Shift's `image` input — pipeline A (Rotate → Shift) is now assembled.

steps.title: Click Shift (A)
steps.body: Click this Shift.

steps.title: Set dx to 40
steps.body: Enter **40** in `dx`. Pipeline A becomes: rotate 30° → shift right 40 px.

steps.title: Pipeline B · drop Shift
steps.body: Now build pipeline B (Shift → Rotate). From Geometry, drag another **Shift**.

steps.title: Wire Checker → Shift (B)
steps.body: Drag Checker's `image` output to the new Shift's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `geom.shift`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline before we set the same dx as pipeline A.

steps.title: Click Shift (B)
steps.body: Click the new Shift.

steps.title: Set dx to 40 (same)
steps.body: Enter **40** in `dx` — identical to pipeline A for a fair comparison.

steps.title: Pipeline B · drop Rotate
steps.body: Drag another **Rotate**. Place it after Shift (B).

steps.title: Wire Shift (B) → Rotate (B)
steps.body: Drag Shift (B)'s `image` output to Rotate's `image` input — pipeline B (Shift → Rotate) is now assembled.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `geom.rotate`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline before we set the same angle as pipeline A.

steps.title: Click Rotate (B)
steps.body: Click this Rotate.

steps.title: Set angle_deg to 30 (same)
steps.body: Enter **30** — same conditions as Rotate (A).

steps.title: Drop arith.binop for the A − B diff
steps.body: From Arithmetic, drag **Arithmetic · a ∘ b**. Subtracting A and B visualises the order dependence.

steps.title: Wire Shift (A) → binop.a
steps.body: Drag pipeline A's final Shift node's `image` output to arith.binop's `a` input.

steps.title: Wire Rotate (B) → binop.b
steps.body: Drag pipeline B's final Rotate node's `image` output to the same arith.binop's `b` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. `arith.binop`'s default behaviour becomes a baseline before we flip the op to sub.

steps.title: Click binop
steps.body: Click arith.binop.

steps.title: Set op to sub
steps.body: Change `op` to **`sub`** — output becomes `A − B`.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body:
Press ▶ Run graph. Both pipelines and the diff execute. What to notice:

  1. **Compare the A and B previews** — the checkerboard grid is clearly in different places. A is shifted 40 px right; B's shift direction has been rotated 30° so it lands up-and-right.
  2. **Diff (A − B) preview on binop** — bright/dark bands follow the checker outlines. Amplitude reaches nearly the original dynamic range (0..1) — a direct view of how big the order-violation offset is.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
**Takeaway:** rotation is centre-anchored, translation is in canvas coordinates → `R·T ≠ T·R` (**non-commutative**). When propagating alignment outputs downstream, you must agree on the application order. The SPIDER / RELION convention is **rotate first, translate second** (= pipeline A order).

**Play with it:**
  • Set either `dx` or `angle_deg` to 0 — A − B collapses to zero (order doesn't matter if one of them is identity).
  • Set `angle_deg` to 90 — integer-multiple right-angle rotations still leave a diff (the shift direction after rotation is totally different).
  • Switch arith.binop's `op` to `div` for a ratio visualisation — same shape, different reading.

Next: **Comparison 5 · Rotate N times — accumulating interpolation error** — looks at how splitting the same total rotation across many passes affects interpolation loss.
